title: 7-round AES-256: reported whole-key herd filter, near-codebook cp

display.name: Herd filter, near-codebook CP, full-key headline

target.description: The authors' reported whole-key attack on 7-round AES-256, with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted. The detailed filter stage is separately recorded as aes256-7r-integral-fklssww2001-herd-near-codebook-cp; its selected subkey material and the broader whole-cipher claim have different scopes.

setting.key_relation: One unknown master key with the standard AES expansion; no related-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: Selected near-codebook: four plaintext bytes cover 2^32-2^23 chosen values; the remaining twelve bytes cover every value, totaling 2^128-2^119 distinct plaintexts.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.
Use only undamaged herds after removing the selected 2^23 four-byte values; approximately 2^23 complete three-fixed-byte herds remain.

This record retains the paper's explicit whole-cipher attack headline. The detailed search first isolates selected subkey material; repeated filtering, reverse expansion or residual search for full master-key completion is not separately costed for every endpoint in this version.

time.note: The dominating scan updates one counter for each known/selected text. The paper uses 2^8 memory lookups per trial-encryption equivalent. Data acquisition is not counted as 2^128 new trial encryptions; scan operations and oracle observations remain separate. This whole-key row preserves the authors' attack-level estimate; it does not infer a new constant factor from the separately catalogued filter.

data.note: This is (2^32-2^23)*2^96 selected distinct plaintexts. It is not a random known-plaintext sample. The acquisition budget is the paper's reported attack-level budget.

memory.note: Section 2.5 gives the dominant 2^64 one-bit parity-counter array; later phases have smaller 2^32 counters. The near-codebook change is stated not to alter the attack complexity.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: The exact key_recovery endpoint has no numerical joint success. The zero sum over the entire unpartitioned codebook also holds for wrong guesses and is not a distinguisher; the attack uses correctly partitioned complete herds. The near-codebook construction leaves about half of the herds undamaged, a coverage count rather than a random-selection success rate. The source gives qualitative wrong-hypothesis rejection and an author headline, not a finite-budget probability for all targeted key material. This is an author full-key headline; numerical success of unitemized completion is not inferred from the selected-subkey relation.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit; preserve resource parameters, existing conflicts and full-audit gates. Local source models and conditional relations do not certify whole-output success.

components.description: PDF6–9 Sections2.5–2.6: within a complete herd formed using the correct initial key hypothesis, the targeted byte of b5 sums to zero. For near-codebook data this is conditional on selecting an undamaged herd; it is not a claim about randomly choosing one.
